questions.prompt: According to integrated information theory (IIT), what does the quantity $\Phi$ (phi) measure?

options.text: How much integrated information a system generates as a whole, beyond what its parts generate independently
How widely a piece of information is broadcast across the brain
options.why_wrong: Wide broadcast is the core idea of global workspace theory, not IIT.

options.text: The total number of neurons active at a given moment
options.why_wrong: IIT is about the cause-effect structure of a system, not a count of active units.

options.text: How strongly a system represents its own mental states
options.why_wrong: Representing one's own states is the core idea of higher-order theories.

questions.explanation: IIT proposes that consciousness corresponds to integrated information, quantified as $\Phi$: information generated by the system as a whole that is lost when it is cut into independent parts.

sources.citation: Tononi, G. (2004). An information integration theory of consciousness. BMC Neuroscience, 5, 42.
Oizumi, M., Albantakis, L., & Tononi, G. (2014). From the phenomenology to the mechanisms of consciousness: Integrated Information Theory 3.0. PLoS Computational Biology, 10(5), e1003588.

questions.prompt: Which neuroscientist first proposed integrated information theory?
questions.explanation: Tononi introduced the theory in the early 2000s and has developed it with colleagues through several versions, including IIT 3.0 (2014).

sources.citation: Tononi, G. (2004). An information integration theory of consciousness. BMC Neuroscience, 5, 42.
Oizumi, M., Albantakis, L., & Tononi, G. (2014). From the phenomenology to the mechanisms of consciousness: Integrated Information Theory 3.0. PLoS Computational Biology, 10(5), e1003588.

questions.prompt: IIT starts from axioms said to be true of every experience. Which of these is one of them?

options.text: Integration: each experience is unified and cannot be reduced to independent components
Broadcast: conscious contents are made available to many processes at once
options.why_wrong: This describes global workspace theory, not an IIT axiom.

options.text: Reportability: an experience exists only if it can be reported
options.why_wrong: IIT explicitly does not tie consciousness to report.

options.text: Metarepresentation: a state is conscious when another state represents it
options.why_wrong: This is the core claim of higher-order theories.

questions.explanation: IIT 3.0 lists five axioms about experience: intrinsic existence, composition, information, integration and exclusion. It then asks what physical properties a system needs to account for each.

sources.citation: Oizumi, M., Albantakis, L., & Tononi, G. (2014). From the phenomenology to the mechanisms of consciousness: Integrated Information Theory 3.0. PLoS Computational Biology, 10(5), e1003588.
Tononi, G., Boly, M., Massimini, M., & Koch, C. (2016). Integrated information theory: from consciousness to its physical substrate. Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 17, 450-461.

questions.prompt: In integrated information theory, which Greek letter names the measure of integrated information?
questions.explanation: IIT quantifies integrated information with $\Phi$ (phi): how much information a system generates as a whole beyond its parts.

sources.citation: Tononi, G. (2004). An information integration theory of consciousness. BMC Neuroscience, 5, 42.
